original_annotations.instruction: On Wikipedia, open the article for the specific seed used to coat the dough in the video and verify whether it is recognized as a major food allergen in the United States.

observed_events.description: The wearer portions dough, works near the bakery roller and arranges relatively short straight pieces in rows.
The wearer hand-rolls a later piece into a long thin strand, bends adjacent loops and presses them together. No end-through-loop knot is established.

visual_review.scope_limit: Corrected from independent dense continuous inventory: hand rolling and adjacent folds are visible; exact knot topology, recipe, regional bread name and measured length are not proved.

unsupported_claims: The two shapes use different dough recipes.
The straight pieces and knots have a particular regional bread name.
The visible seed coating is required by either digital resource.
Any public tutorial is already known to satisfy either shape.
The later folds are a single or double knot.

parent_recording_evidence.note: Official upstream entry verified on 2026-10-17. Runtime lineage resolves this same media UUID through the canonical mapping; original_video_id is retained as the upstream clip identifier.

redistribution_permission_evidence.finding: The official Ego4D page requires signing a Data Usage Agreement. The linked draft distinguishes limited research/publication uses from third-party dataset access or redistribution. The Ego2Web API returned no license card. Neither proves that this project signed the applicable agreement or obtained permission to redistribute this source in a benchmark.
redistribution_permission_evidence.required_evidence: An applicable signed agreement or explicit rights-holder permission covering the intended benchmark source distribution; do not infer it from possession of the clip.

instruction_freeze.rule: Keep A, fixed B and the bundled instruction unchanged during retrieval and answer selection.

screening.real_user_need: Switch from learning the first batch’s shape to practising even thickness in the later hand-rolling preparation.
screening.before: One beginner guide for shaping the first straight batch.
screening.later_information: The user wants to practise the preparation step before folding the later batch and reports difficulty getting an even thickness.
screening.after: Keep one verified hand-rolling preparation guide; remove a separate first-batch-only lesson. A guide that also teaches the later step remains acceptable.

supported_claims.text: First batch: shorter straight dough pieces arranged in rows.
Later batch: dough is hand-rolled into a long thin strand before adjacent folds. The user requests help obtaining more even thickness.

construct.research_question: Can an Agent revise the learning goal from a first shape to a practical difficulty in preparing the later dough batch?
construct.belief_before: One beginner guide to form the observed straight dough portions; a usable shaping segment inside a longer recipe qualifies.
construct.belief_after: One guide that teaches later hand-rolling preparation; initial-only log folding/sealing no longer qualifies.
construct.required_behavior_change: Re-evaluate the saved guide against the preparation need; keep a qualifying guide or select another supported preparation lesson, without keeping an extra video.
construct.no_update_failure: Keep an initial-only folding/sealing lesson without later hand-rolling preparation.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: Scene supplies the dough, hand-rolling method and position before folding. Uneven-thickness difficulty is user-authored need; recipe, seed, measured length and exact knot are not inferred.

instructions.a: Save one beginner tutorial to help me shape the first batch I make here.
instructions.b: Actually, I want to practise the preparation step for the later batch before I start folding it. I struggle to get the thickness even. Save one guide for that instead of the first-batch shaping lesson.
instructions.bundled: Save one guide to help me get an even thickness in the preparation step for the later batch, before folding it. Do not keep a separate first-batch shaping lesson.

native_state_checks.wrong: Only a slab-cut shortcut, industrial forming advert or braid-only lesson.

initial_goal_review.reason: The first batch is short rounded straight dough, processed through a roller and arranged on the board. All final hand-rolling methods can help form a straight portion. A straight-log shaping segment also qualifies when followed by filling, coiling, cutting or knotting; no recipe/size restriction is invented. Folding a flat portion into a log and sealing it helps initial shape but does not teach later palm elongation. Round-only, flat-sheet-only, cut-strip/twist-only, ready-strand braiding, bulk mixing and unrelated materials do not teach the observed first shape.
